body.statement: For every \(N\ge4\), the rational family \(x^{(N)}\) lies in \([0,1]^{3\times N}\) and satisfies \(V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=(324N-305)/(230400N)\), \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)=(324N-300)/(230400N)\), and \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=1/(46080N)\). Its core dual-tight face has a unique feasible solution with eight positive cell counts equal to \(1/2\); every integral core completion has dual slack at least \(5\), and an explicit pair of permutations attains slack \(5\). Dummy rows are isolated by strictly positive mixed-cell slack.
body.justification: An all-\(N\) rational obstruction proves that the upper rate cannot be improved and eliminates replication-parity ambiguity.
body.gap: Emami and Pass (2025, Example 1) and Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2) exhibit fixed-size non-Monge plans, but not a bounded scalar signed-contrast family with exact \(1/N\) loss for every large population size.
body.consumer: The family certifies that fractional causal variance endpoints can overstate the realizable endpoint by order \(N^{-2}\) after the randomization-variance scaling.
body.proof_tex:
Use zero-based indices for the four core atoms and set
\[
 s_{ijk}=A_{1i}+A_{2j}+A_{3k},\qquad
 d_{ijk}=s_{ijk}^2-u_{1i}-u_{2j}-u_{3k}.
\]
For fixed first-coordinate indices \(i=0,1,2,3\), the four exact slack matrices, with rows indexed by \(j\) and columns by \(k\), are
\[
\begin{gathered}
\begin{pmatrix}144&279&479&999\\45&120&260&660\\185&60&0&0\\245&420&660&1260\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}35&0&30&210\\140&45&15&75\\960&665&435&95\\0&5&75&335\end{pmatrix},\\[3pt]
\begin{pmatrix}156&51&11&51\\345&180&80&0\\1445&1080&780&300\\65&0&0&120\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}0&15&95&375\\45&0&20&180\\665&420&240&0\\5&60&180&540\end{pmatrix}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Thus the displayed \(u\)'s are dual feasible for the unshifted squared-sum cost, the smallest positive core slack is \(5\), and the zero-slack cells are
\[
 022,023,101,130,213,231,232,300,311,323.
\]
Give each of the four core atoms marginal count \(m\), and denote the counts on these ten cells in the displayed order by \(t_0,\ldots,t_9\).  The arm-2 label-2 equation minus the arm-1 label-0 equation gives \(t_9=0\).  The arm-3 label-3 and arm-1 label-0 equations then give \(t_4=t_0\).  The arm-2 label-1 and arm-3 label-2 equations give \(t_8=t_6=t_1\).  Subtracting the arm-2 label-3 equation from the arm-1 label-2 equation gives \(t_3=t_4=t_0\).  The arm-1 label-1 and arm-2 label-0 equations give \(t_2=t_1\) and \(t_7=t_0\).  The arm-3 label-0 equation is \(t_3+t_7=m\), hence \(2t_0=m\); finally the arm-1 label-2 equation forces \(t_5=0\).  Since \(t_0+t_1=m\), the unique feasible zero-slack table is
\[
 (t_0,\ldots,t_9)
 =(m/2,m/2,m/2,m/2,m/2,0,m/2,m/2,m/2,0).
\]
For \(m=1\), it has eight positive half-counts.  Directly from the displayed arrays and cells,
\[
 \sum_i u_{1i}+\sum_j u_{2j}+\sum_k u_{3k}=502-207-240=55,
\]
and its primal cost is
\[
 \frac12(4+64+4+1+16+16+4+1)=55.
\]
Thus its unshifted primal and dual objectives both equal \(55\).

Add a dummy atom \((100,100,-200)\) with dual potential zero in each arm.  Mixed cells remain strictly dual-slack.  Indeed, according as the dummy-coordinate set is \(\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\), the slack is bounded below respectively by
\[
 71^2,\quad 78^2-184,\quad171^2-184,
 \quad187^2,\quad86^2,\quad85^2-184.
\]
The first value is \(5041\), and every other displayed value is larger.  The all-dummy cell has cost and dual value zero.  Therefore the half-count core table together with \(N-4\) all-dummy rows proves that the unshifted fractional optimum is \(55\).

Any integral completion containing a mixed cell has total dual slack at least \(5041\).  Without a mixed cell, all dummy occurrences form all-dummy rows and the remaining four rows constitute an integral core table.  The unique zero-slack core table above is not integral, so at least one core cell has positive slack, at least \(5\).  Conversely, relative to the first arm, the permutations
\[
 \sigma_2=(2,0,1,3),\qquad \sigma_3=(2,1,3,0)
\]
give rows \(022,101,213,330\) of unshifted squared costs \(4,4,16,36\), totaling \(60=55+5\).  Appending all-dummy rows proves that the unshifted integral optimum is exactly \(60\).

It remains to translate this certificate to the bounded outcomes in def:lower-family.  Their transformed coordinates satisfy
\[
 c_1x_1=\frac{A_1+9}{480},\qquad
 c_2x_2=\frac{A_2+16}{480},\qquad
 c_3x_3=\frac{A_3-7}{480}.
\]
All core and dummy outcomes lie in \([0,1]\).  If \(s\) denotes an unshifted row sum, then the actual row cost is \((s+18)^2/480^2\).  The sum of \(s\) over every feasible coupling is the fixed marginal sum
\[
 \sum_i A_{1i}+\sum_iA_{2i}+\sum_iA_{3i}=-10,
\]
because each dummy row has unshifted sum zero.  Hence every feasible total objective is transformed by
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^N(s_r+18)^2
 =\sum_{r=1}^Ns_r^2+36(-10)+324N.
\]
The fractional and integral total numerators are consequently \(324N-305\) and \(324N-300\).  Division by \(N\cdot480^2=230400N\) gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=\frac{324N-305}{230400N},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)=\frac{324N-300}{230400N},
\]
and their difference is \(1/(46080N)\), for every \(N\ge4\).  This is an explicit same-class rational witness, with no parity restriction.
